methodology: The decomposition process involved breaking down both the original research topic and the generated technical specification into their fundamental components. Each component was analyzed for independence, specificity, and implementability. The original research topic was dissected into atomic units that represent distinct requirements, features, and behaviors necessary for the 12-hour clock design. Similarly, the generated specification was parsed to extract atomic units that describe the implementation details, logic functions, and operational characteristics of the clock module. The criteria for atomic units included ensuring that each unit is self-contained, technically specific, and can be implemented as a single requirement without ambiguity.
mindtraced_atomic_units: Create a set of counters suitable for use as a 12-hour clock with an AM/PM indicator.
Counters are clocked by a high-frequency clk signal.
Increment pulse on ena occurs once per second.
pm signal indicates whether the time is in PM or AM.
hh, mm, and ss are represented as two BCD digits each.
Minutes (mm) and seconds (ss) range from 00 to 59.
Reset signal is active high and resets the clock to '12:00 AM'.
Reset has higher priority than enable and can occur at any time.
spec_atomic_units: The top module header defines inputs clk, reset, ena, and outputs pm, hh, mm, ss.
The combinational logic for the 12-hour clock module is based on BCD representation.
Each counter (hh, mm, ss) operates independently and increments based on the ena signal.
Seconds counter (ss) counts from 00 to 59 and resets to 00 after reaching 59.
Minutes counter (mm) counts from 00 to 59 and resets to 00 after reaching 59.
Hours counter (hh) counts from 01 to 12 and resets to 01 after reaching 12.
pm output is set high when hour counter indicates 12 PM and low for 12 AM.
Reset signal has the highest priority and sets all counters to initial state when activated.
Enable signal controls the incrementing of the counters based on clk cycles.
Outputs hh, mm, and ss are represented in BCD format.
